classification.difficultyReason: Select corresponding triangles around intersecting diagonals and combine known bisection, vertical and alternate angles into a standard AAS argument and matching-side conclusion.

content.prompt: The diagonals of the parallelogram $ABCD$ intersect at $O$. A line through $O$ meets the sides $AB$ and $CD$ at $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Prove that $OX=OY$.

spec.description: Complete source figure, incidences and marks preserved; houseblack10pt labels.

answer.worked: Since parallelogram diagonals bisect each other, $OB=OD$. Also $\angle BOX=\angle DOY$ (vertically opposite angles), and $\angle OBX=\angle ODY$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$). Thus $\triangle BOX\cong\triangle DOY$ by AAS. Corresponding sides give $OX=OY$.
